title: Climbing to survive: Potential elevational shifts in warming risk for the Moltrecht's treefrog
content:
Low-elevation populations of Zhangixalus moltrechti had higher thermal limits but lower warming tolerance than high-elevation populations. Climate change is expected to expand high-risk areas upslope, highlighting the need for emissions reduction and targeted habitat management.


Abstract

Climate change poses a growing threat to biodiversity, particularly to ectothermic organisms such as amphibians. Understanding geographic variation in thermal tolerance and warming tolerance can provide insights into population responses to climate change and potential future distributional shifts. We examined warming tolerance patterns across an elevational gradient in the endemic Taiwanese treefrog Zhangixalus moltrechti (Boulenger, 1908). We integrated critical thermal maximum (CTmax) measurements from nine populations spanning an elevational gradient with species distribution models and topographic data to estimate current and future spatial patterns of warming tolerance across the species' potentially suitable range under different greenhouse gas emission scenarios. Although low-elevation populations exhibited higher CTmax, they had lower warming tolerance than high-elevation populations. Under SSP5–8.5, the proportion of the species' range exposed to extreme warming risk, defined as a warming tolerance below 10°C, is projected to increase from approximately 26% at present to 48% by the 2050s and 65% by the 2070s. The upper elevational boundary of this risk zone is projected to shift upwards from approximately 483 m at present to 775 m by the 2050s and 1528 m by the 2070s. Practical implication: Despite its broad elevational distribution, Z. moltrechti may face substantial climate-related threats, particularly at lower elevations. Reducing greenhouse gas emissions is essential for limiting the expansion of high-warming-risk areas. Targeted management in high-risk regions, such as increasing canopy cover around breeding water bodies to reduce heat exposure and provide thermal refuges, may further help protect vulnerable populations.

摘要

氣候變遷對生物多樣性構成日益嚴重的威脅，尤其是兩棲類等外溫動物。了解熱耐受性與暖化耐受性在地理空間上的變異，有助於掌握不同族群對氣候變遷的反應，並預測其未來可能的分布變化。 本研究探討臺灣特有種莫氏樹蛙 Zhangixalus moltrechti (Boulenger, 1908) 沿海拔梯度的暖化耐受性模式。 我們整合九個不同海拔族群的臨界高溫(critical thermal maximum, CTmax)測量結果、物種分布模型，以及地形資料，估算不同暖化情景與年份下，其潛在分布範圍內的暖化風險的變化。 儘管低海拔族群具有較高的 CTmax，其暖化耐受性仍低於高海拔族群。在 SSP5-8.5 情境下，物種分布範圍內面臨極高暖化風險的區域比例(定義為暖化耐受性低於 10°C 的區域)預計將由目前的約 26%，增加至 2050 年代的 48%及2070 年代的 65%。此風險區域的海拔上限預計將由目前約 483 m，向上移升至 2050 年代的 775 m及2070 年代的 1,528 m。 實際意義:儘管莫氏樹蛙具有廣泛的海拔分布範圍，氣候變遷仍可能對其部分族群造成威脅。降低溫室氣體排放能夠減緩其高暖化風險棲地擴張。此外，針對高風險區域採取適當的棲地管理措施，例如增加繁殖水體周圍的樹冠覆蓋，以降低熱暴露並提供熱庇護所，可能有助於保護易受影響的族群。
